BiblicalUsage: Ashima is named once, as the god of Hamath, one of the peoples the king of Assyria settles in the cities of Samaria. Every nation makes gods of their own, the men of Hamath make Ashima, and they set them in the high places the Samaritans had made.
TheologicalSignificance: A god named once for a people moved into Samaria tells me how the land filled with idols: each nation brings its own, and the high places hold them all side by side.
